drupalComments.body:
Would somebody please consider launching this Change.org petition?

I'd really appreciate it if someone else in the chart community would be willing to start a Change.org petition, because I'm not planning to do it myself.

The petition would ask the Official Charts Company to modernize the UK Singles Chart and Official Albums Chart by separating current releases from catalogue releases.

The proposal would be:

  • From this year onward, only songs and albums released within the previous two calendar years should be eligible for the main Official Singles and Albums Charts. That means songs and albums released in 2024 or earlier would no longer be eligible for the main charts.
  • Instead, all songs and albums released in 2024 or earlier would move to two new permanent charts:
    • Official Legacy Singles Chart
    • Official Legacy Albums Chart
  • Beginning in 2027, the cut-off would move forward by one year, meaning songs and albums released in 2025 or earlier would move to the Legacy Charts. The eligibility window would continue to roll forward every year after that.
  • All greatest hits, best of, and compilation albums, regardless of when they were released, would always chart on the Official Legacy Albums Chart rather than the main albums chart.

The aim would not be to erase older music. Classic songs and albums deserve recognition and should continue to have official charts dedicated to them. Instead, the goal would be to ensure that the main UK charts primarily reflect the success of today's new releases while still celebrating catalogue music through dedicated legacy rankings.

The Official Charts Company already operates dozens of specialist charts alongside the main Singles and Albums Charts, so creating two additional Legacy Charts would fit within the existing chart ecosystem. Any change to chart eligibility would ultimately be a matter for the Official Charts Company and the Chart Supervisory Committee, which regularly review and approve the official chart rules.

If anyone genuinely supports this idea and has the time to organize it, please feel free to launch a Change.org petition yourself. I'm simply sharing the idea—I won't be creating or running the petition.
